newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX stuck at higher levels before U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: German DAX stuck at higher levels before U.S. data.

text.p: German shares on Tuesday closed at higher levels reached earlier after Wall Street's overnight gains, but were unable to build on that firmness as caution ahead of U.S. consumer price data due later set in.
Dealers said the German market was above all concerned that the figures would show inflationary pressure that could in turn heighten the outlook for a further rise in U.S. interest rates.

The 30-share DAX index ended up 47.78 points at 3,327.68 points, or a gain of 1.46 percent. The index had earlier reached a daily high of 3,337.01 points, while June DAX futures traded up 31.5 points at 3,339.5 points.

The strength of the dollar, maintaining a level above 1.73 marks, together with higher German debt prices, continued to lend support before the U.S. data due at 1230 GMT. The earliest likely opportunity for a U.S. rate movement would be at the Federal Reserve's next meeting in May.

Some traders said the German market would in the meantime be underpinned by domestic fundamentals, including the weaker mark and relatively low interest rates, and that the DAX should remain between 3,200 and 3,400 points in the near-term.
Carmaker shares were at the forefront, with both BMW AG and Daimler AG both posting gains based on support from the dollar.

The gains came despite the European car manufacturers' association ACEA saying on Tuesday that west European car registrations fell three percent year-on-year in March to 1.24 million units, with market leader VW posting no growth.
Its shares, after rising strongly early on, closed 11 marks down at 1,039.0.

Truckmaker and engineering group MAN also outpaced the market, with traders noting an aggressive buyer of MAN shares in early dealings and the stronger dollar. Its shares closed 26.30 marks up at 504.30.
Among other top performers, engineering group Linde AG rose 54 marks to 1,160 marks, while software group SAP rose 10.90 marks to 286.20 marks.

Adidas was up 4.20 marks at 186 marks after the sportswear group said it would seek shareholder approval for a capital rights issue. Rival Puma AG also rose as the two groups outpaced the overall market gain.
